user.name: Charley Dunkel
user.backstory: Charley's weather app works now, and it's saved on GitHub. Next up: a dark mode. But Charley doesn't want to risk breaking the version that already works.

cards.title: What is a branch?
body: A branch is a separate line of snapshots. Think of it as a second save slot in a game: you can try something risky there, and your main save stays safe. Every project starts with one branch, called `main`.

cards.title: Make a branch and move onto it
body: `git switch -c add-dark-mode` creates a new branch called `add-dark-mode` and moves you onto it. The `-c` means "create." From now on, new snapshots go on this branch, and `main` isn't touched.
Older tutorials use `git checkout -b add-dark-mode`, which does the same thing.

cards.title: See your branches
body: `git branch` lists all your branches. The one with a `*` next to it is the branch you're on right now.

questions.prompt: Why would Charley make a branch for dark mode?
options: To upload the project to GitHub

questions.prompt: When you run `git branch`, what does the `*` mean?
options: That's the branch you're on right now
questions.wrongFeedback: The `*` marks the branch you're currently on.
